newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-HARADA GETS NAGANO BOOST WITH WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-HARADA GETS NAGANO BOOST WITH WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Japanese Masahiko Harada warmed up for the Nagano Olympics in style by winning the high hill ski jumping at the Nordic skiing world championships on Saturday.
Harada, who won two silvers in the normal hill event and in the team jumping, completed his collection of medals with a gold.
"This will boost my confidence for Nagano," he said, already dreaming of a triumph before his fans at next year's Winter Games.

The 28-year-old from Kamikawa took the lead with a first jump at 124 metres and sealed victory by setting the day's best mark with a second jump at 128 metres to score a winning total of 252.1 points.
German Dieter Thoma, fourth in the provisional standings after a first jump at 121.5 points, hoped for gold after a second jump at 124 metres.
But Harada did not crack under pressure and Thoma had to be content with second place on 244.5 points.
Thoma has enjoyed success on the World Cup circuit but had never won a medal in an individual event of a major competition.
He would have won gold in last week's normal hill competition had he not fallen after landing his second jump.
"It's good to win a medal at last," he said. "I knew I was in great shape and capable of taking one but I've been so unlucky in the past that I wasn't sure I would make it."
Sylvain Freiholz of Switzerland was ninth after the first round but a second jump at 123.5 metres lifted him to third place on 237.3 points.

Austrian Andreas Goldberger, who has won three overall World Cup titles but not a single world title, will have to keep waiting as a poor first jump at 90.5 metres did not allow him to qualify for the second round.
There was disappointment also for Slovenian teenager Primoz Peterka, who burst into the limelight by winning the coveted Four Hills tournament last month, as he could do no better than 13th.
Harada said he drew inspiration from the huge crowd lining the 120-metre hill on a mild day with hardly any wind.
"All the people who had come for the cross-country stayed for the ski jumping," he said. "The atmosphere was great and I really wanted to jump far to thank them for coming."
Asked if he expected such a big crowd in Nagano, Harada smiled: "Of course, I'm a star in Japan," he said.
